316951.title: Ito–Terwilliger parameter-array existence and uniqueness conjecture for sharp tridiagonal systems
316951.literal:
Let $d$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\mathbb{K}$ be a field, and let

$$
(\{\theta_i\}_{i=0}^d;\{\theta_i^*\}_{i=0}^d;\{\zeta_i\}_{i=0}^d)
$$

be a sequence of scalars in $\mathbb{K}$. A **sharp tridiagonal system** is a tridiagonal system whose associated endpoint eigenspace is one-dimensional; its displayed scalar data are called its **parameter array**. **Ito–Terwilliger's parameter-array conjecture.** There exists a sharp tridiagonal system $\Phi$ over $\mathbb{K}$ with this parameter array if and only if: (i) $\theta_i\ne\theta_j$ and $\theta_i^*\ne\theta_j^*$ whenever $i\ne j$; (ii) $\zeta_0=1$, $\zeta_d\ne0$, and

$$
\sum_{i=0}^d \eta_{d-i}(\theta_0)\eta^*_{d-i}(\theta_0^*)\zeta_i\ne0;
$$

(iii) the quantities

$$
\frac{\theta_{i-2}-\theta_{i+1}}{\theta_{i-1}-\theta_i},\qquad
\frac{\theta^*_{i-2}-\theta^*_{i+1}}{\theta^*_{i-1}-\theta^*_i}
$$

are equal and independent of $i$ for $2\le i\le d-1$. Whenever these conditions hold, $\Phi$ is unique up to isomorphism of tridiagonal systems. The conjecture would characterize exactly which scalar data arise from sharp tridiagonal systems and would give their uniqueness from the parameter array; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
316951.derivation_and_gap: Need existence over EVERY field for every admissible parameter array and full isomorphism uniqueness. Split-eigenvalue conditions and low-d matrix realizations do not pay arbitrary diameter or bad characteristic. Possible public classification must be checked in actual primary bodies; not done.

324593.title: Cameron–Sheehan–Spiga conjecture on semiregular automorphisms of cubic vertex-transitive graphs
324593.literal:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite, connected graph with no loops or multiple edges. It is **cubic** if it is regular of valency $3$, and **vertex-transitive** if $\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)$ acts transitively on its vertices. An automorphism is **semiregular** if, in its action on the vertices, all cycles in its disjoint cycle decomposition have the same length.

**Cameron–Sheehan–Spiga conjecture.** There exists a function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty} f(n)=\infty
$$

such that, if $\Gamma$ is a cubic vertex-transitive graph with $n$ vertices, then $\Gamma$ has a semiregular automorphism of order at least $f(n)$.

The conjecture predicts that the order of a semiregular automorphism in a cubic vertex-transitive graph must become arbitrarily large as the number of vertices grows. The source states that it holds when $\Gamma$ is either a Cayley graph or an arc-transitive graph, while the general case is presented as open.
324593.derivation_and_gap: Need a uniform diverging semiregular order for all cubic vertex-transitive graphs, not only Cayley/arc-transitive cases. Neither a bounded-order automorphism family nor group-action reduction was obtained; primary and later classification unread.

325155.title: The bounded Freiman ring-isomorphism conjecture over finite fields
325155.literal:
Let $k\geq 3$ be an integer. A bijection preserving the vanishing of every $k$-bounded integer polynomial is called an **$F_k$-ring-isomorphism**. For a prime $p$, write $\mathbb{F}_p$ for the finite field with $p$ elements. A subset of a characteristic-zero integral domain is one contained in such a domain. **Bounded Freiman ring-isomorphism conjecture.** For any $k\geq 3$, there is an infinite sequence of prime numbers such that, for each prime $p$ in the sequence, there exists a subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p$ with

$$
|A|=O(\log\log p)
$$

which is not $F_k$-ring-isomorphic to any subset of a characteristic-zero integral domain. The preceding theorem gives a larger bound of order $\log p/\log\log p$; the conjecture asks whether substantially smaller obstructing subsets exist along an infinite sequence of primes.
325155.derivation_and_gap: Need infinitely many primes with O(log log p)-sized characteristic-zero obstruction under the exact k-bounded polynomial definition. Iterated squaring creates huge integers but supplies no required large prime factors without a number-theoretic lemma. Metadata says solved; actual source proof unread, so not authenticated as public exclusion.

326540.title: Benevides–Griffiths–Przykucki conjecture on maximum percolation time
326540.literal:
Let $M^d(n)$ denote the maximum percolation time in two-dimensional bootstrap percolation on the $d$-dimensional grid $[n]^d$. For fixed $d\geq 1$, the conjecture is

$$
M^d(n)=\frac{6d^2-5d-1}{18}n^2+O(n).
$$

**Benevides–Griffiths–Przykucki conjecture.** For all fixed $d\geq 1$,

$$
M^d(n)=\frac{6d^2-5d-1}{18}n^2+O(n).
$$

The lower bound is sharp for $d=2$, where it gives the constant $13/18$; the conjecture asserts that the same asymptotic formula gives the maximum percolation time in every fixed dimension.
326540.derivation_and_gap: Need all fixed dimensions, exact quadratic coefficient and O(n) remainder. A slow percolating sequence in one slice supplies only a lower bound and may be accelerated by cross-slice neighbors. No matching all-dimensional causal infection upper bound or counterfamily.

330958.title: Orientation conjecture for triangulations on orientable surfaces
330958.literal:
Let $T$ be a triangulation on an orientable surface of genus $g\geq 1$. An orientation of $T$ is an assignment of a direction to each edge; its outdegree at a vertex is the number of edges directed away from that vertex. The **dual orientation** is the orientation of the dual graph induced by the orientation of $T$, and a cycle is **non-contractible** if it cannot be continuously shrunk to a point on the surface.

**Orientation conjecture.** $T$ admits an orientation of its edges such that every vertex has outdegree at least $3$, divisible by $3$, and such that there is no oriented non-contractible cycle in the dual orientation.

The statement would extend the known result for simple triangulations to all triangulations and provide the orientation property needed to generalize the encoding method to higher-genus surfaces. The source presents it as a hoped-for generalization; its resolution is not given here.
330958.derivation_and_gap: Need positive outdegrees divisible by three AND dual noncontractible-cycle exclusion on every permitted triangulation. Vertex splitting may create low-degree vertices and alter dual homotopy. Definitions of loops and contractible separators unpaid; no domain correction credited.

332419.title: Asymptotic coincidence of Hamming bounds for unrestricted data-syndrome codes
332419.literal:
Let $d$ be the minimum distance and let $n$ denote the block length. The Hamming bound for non-degenerate data-syndrome codes is the bound in equation (HBnondeg), while unrestricted data-syndrome codes satisfy the bound in equation (HBdeg).

**Asymptotic Hamming-bound conjecture.** For any $d$ there exists $n(d)$ such that for $n\geq n(d)$ the Hamming bound in equation (HBnondeg) holds for unrestricted data-syndrome codes.

The authors report that the two bounds coincide for $n\geq 36$ when $d=7$, and observe the same behavior for other values of $d$. The conjecture asserts that this eventual coincidence holds for every fixed minimum distance.
332419.derivation_and_gap: Need the actual two Hamming-bound expressions and uniform eventual comparison for every fixed distance under unrestricted degeneracy. Leading-term comparison alone may fail at the maximizing auxiliary Krawtchouk index; equations and source proof unpaid.

334768.title: Optimal sparse blow-up conjecture for bounded-bandwidth graphs
334768.literal:
For each $\gamma>0$, $\Delta\ge2$, and $k\ge1$, there should exist constants $\beta^\ast>0$ and $C^\ast>0$ such that, asymptotically almost surely for $\Gamma=G(n,p)$ whenever $p\ge C^\ast n^{-2/(\Delta+2)}$, every spanning subgraph $G$ of $\Gamma$ with

$$
\delta(G)\ge\left(\frac{k-1}{k}+\gamma\right)pn
$$

and every $k$-colourable graph $H$ on $n$ vertices with $\Delta(H)\le\Delta$, bandwidth at most $\beta^\ast n$, at least $C^\ast p^{-2}$ vertices not contained in any triangles, and at least $C^\ast p^{-(\Delta+2)(\Delta-1)/2}n^{2-\Delta}$ vertices not contained in any $K_{\Delta+1}$, satisfy the following. **Sparse blow-up conjecture.** The graph $G$ contains a copy of $H$. This conjecture proposes the expected optimal lower bound on $p$, accounting for the necessary obstructions caused by vertices of $H$ outside triangles and copies of $K_{\Delta+1}$.
334768.derivation_and_gap: Need spanning embedding at the precise sparse threshold and both exceptional-vertex counts uniformly over all eligible H and G. Almost-spanning claims in metadata do not imply spanning. No absorbing/resilience argument or admissible obstructing family.

339226.title: The higher-dimensional zero-dimensional count formula in dimensions divisible by four
339226.literal:
Let $d\geq4$ with $d\equiv0\pmod4$, let $\ell\in\mathbb{Z}$, and let $L=\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}^d}\otimes t_d^{-\ell}$ be the trivial equivariant line bundle. Let $T$ be the Calabi–Yau subtorus, let $[Z]\in\operatorname{Hilb}^n(\mathbb{C}^d)^T$ correspond to a $(d-1)$-partition $\pi$, and let $o(\mathcal{L})$ be an orientation. **Higher-dimensional count conjecture.** After specializing $\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_{d-1}=\lambda_d=0$, one has

$$
(-1)^{o(\mathcal{L})|_Z}\sqrt{(-1)^n\frac{e_T(\operatorname{Ext}^{\mathrm{even}}(I_Z,I_Z)_0)}{e_T(\operatorname{Ext}^{\mathrm{odd}}(I_Z,I_Z)_0)}}\,e_T(L^{[n]}|_Z)=(-1)^{|\pi|}\omega_\pi\prod_{i=1}^{\pi_{1\ldots1}}(\ell-(i-1)),
$$

for some $\omega_\pi\in\mathbb{Q}$, and there is a choice of orientation on each Hilbert scheme such that

$$
1+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}Z_n(\mathbb{C}^d,L,o(\mathcal{L}))q^n\Big|_{\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_{d-1}=\lambda_d=0}=M_{d-2}(-q)^\ell.
$$

This extends the dimension-four formula to dimensions divisible by four, but is only supported by calculations in the paper; the specialization is also part of the asserted formula.
339226.derivation_and_gap: All d divisible by four needs equivariant Ext Euler-weight specialization and a coherent orientation making the full generating series correct. No exact failing partition or all-partition identity supplied. Primary geometry unread; a low-n calculation would not settle scope.

339479.title: Conjecture on large co-edge-regular graphs with four eigenvalues
339479.literal:
Let $\Gamma$ be a connected co-edge-regular graph with four distinct eigenvalues. Let $t\geq 2$ be an integer and write $|V(\Gamma)|=n(\Gamma)$. An **$s$-clique extension** is a graph obtained from a graph by replacing each vertex with a clique of size $s$, with adjacency between cliques determined by adjacency of the corresponding original vertices. **Large co-edge-regular graph conjecture.** There exists a constant $n_t$ such that, if

$$
\theta_{\min}(\Gamma)\geq -t \quad\text{and}\quad n(\Gamma)\geq n_t,
$$

then $\Gamma$ is the $s$-clique extension of a strongly regular graph for some integer $s$ satisfying $2\leq s\leq t-1$. This predicts a structural classification of sufficiently large connected co-edge-regular graphs in this spectral range; the source presents it as a belief motivated by the study of regular graphs with four distinct eigenvalues and gives no resolution.
339479.derivation_and_gap: See 339479-ORDINARY-AND-PUBLIC.md: personally derived full join-of-pentagons negation, but actual June2026 primary Theorem5.3 gives public counterfamilies with a complete target bridge. Zero prospective novelty.

347733.title: The noisy equitable stochastic block model detection conjecture
347733.literal: Let $\bT_\delta$ be the noise operator that rewires $\lfloor\delta n\rfloor$ swaps of a $d$-regular graph, and let $\sG_{n,d,k,\eta}^{\,\mathrm{eq}}$ be the equitable stochastic block model. Write $\widetilde{\sG}^{\,\mathrm{eq}}_{n,d,k,\eta,\delta}$ for the distribution of $\bT_\delta(\bG)$ when $\bG\sim\sG_{n,d,k,\eta}^{\,\mathrm{eq}}$. For fixed $\delta>0$, $\eta\in[-\frac{1}{k-1},1]$, $k\geq2$, and $d<d_{\mathrm{KS}}^{\,\mathrm{eq}}(\eta)$, with $k\mid(1-\eta)d$, **the noisy equitable stochastic block model detection conjecture.** There is no polynomial-time algorithm that, with high probability as $n\to\infty$, distinguishes $\widetilde{\sG}^{\,\mathrm{eq}}_{n,d,k,\eta,\delta}$ from $\sG_{n,d}$. The divisibility condition ensures that the equitable model is defined for an infinite sequence of values of $n$. This conjecture is used as a conditional hardness assumption for results on random regular graphs; the added rewiring noise is stated to be crucial to the conjecture's applicability.
347733.derivation_and_gap: No polynomial-time distinguishing algorithm for the noisy equitable law was constructed and no complexity lower bound proved. Noise destroys exact equitable certificates; unnoised divisibility tests do not settle fixed positive rewiring noise.

348011.title: Perfect-path density conjecture in the hypercube
348011.literal:
Let $Q_d$ be the $d$-dimensional hypercube, and let $P_{d+1}$ denote the vertex set of a path in $Q_d$ with $d+1$ vertices whose endpoints are at Hamming distance $d$. Such a configuration is called a **perfect path**. Let $\pi(H,d)$ denote the maximum asymptotic density of vertex-induced copies of $H$ in subgraphs of large hypercubes.

**Perfect-path density conjecture.** For all $d\geq 3$,

$$
\pi(P_{d+1},d)=\frac{d!}{(d+1)^{d-1}}.
$$

The case $d=3$ is proved in the paper, yielding $\pi(P_4,3)=3/8$. The source also notes that Baber's flag-algebra upper bound for $\pi(P_5,4)$ is consistent with the conjectured value $24/125$.
348011.derivation_and_gap: Need exact all-d induced perfect-path density upper bound, not just an explicit blow-up lower construction. Local path counts correlate across overlapping subcubes. No all-d inequality or rigorously larger density construction obtained; primary definition of pi still unread.

349349.title: The color-critical-edge stability conjecture for saturated graphs
349349.literal:
Let $r\ge 2$ be an integer and let $F$ be a graph with chromatic number $r+1$ and a **color-critical edge**, meaning an edge whose deletion lowers the chromatic number. Let $t_r(n)$ denote the number of edges in the Turán graph with $r$ parts, and let an $F$-saturated graph be an $F$-free graph to which adding any missing edge creates a copy of $F$.

**Color-critical-edge stability conjecture.** Every $F$-saturated graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $t_r(n)-o(n^{\frac{r+1}{r}})$ edges contains a complete $r$-partite subgraph $G'$ on $(1-o(1))n$ vertices.

This is proposed as a weaker version of the general conjecture, restricting $F$ to graphs with a color-critical edge. The paper presents it as an open proposed version; the full conjecture is proved only for certain 3-chromatic graphs under additional hypotheses.
349349.derivation_and_gap: Approximate Turan stability does not provide a complete multipartite subgraph. Need a defect vertex cover of size o(n) from saturation at the n^((r+1)/r) deficit for every color-critical F. Historical general-F neighbor remains incomplete, not an exclusion for this restriction.

349374.title: Injective free-Lie-algebra map from canonical forms to graph cohomology
349374.literal:
Let $\Omega^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{can}}$ be the graded space of canonical differential forms, let $\mathbb{L}(\Omega^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{can}})$ be the free Lie algebra on it, and let $H^n(\mathcal{GC}_2)$ denote the degree-$n$ cohomology of the graph complex. Let $\omega^{4k+1}$, for $k\geq 1$, denote the primitive canonical forms. **Graph-cohomology conjecture.** There is a non-canonical injective map of graded Lie algebras

$$
\mathbb{L}(\Omega^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{can}})\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb Z}H^n(\mathcal{GC}_2)
$$

whose restriction to the Lie subalgebra generated by the primitive elements maps to the Lie subalgebra of degree-zero cohomology:

$$
\mathbb{L}\left(\bigoplus_{k\geq 1}\omega^{4k+1}\,\mathbb Q\right)\longrightarrow H^0(\mathcal{GC}_2).
$$

All other elements map to higher-degree cohomology $\bigoplus_{n>0}H^n(\mathcal{GC}_2)$. The grading on the source is by differential-form degree, while the grading on the target is by edge number alone; the degree and loop-number gradings on the target are to be forgotten. This conjecture proposes a non-canonical Lie-algebraic relationship between canonical differential forms and graph cohomology, motivated by graph-integral calculations and their motivic-period analogues; the source does not report a proof or disproof.
349374.derivation_and_gap: Need faithful free-Lie classes, including all nonprimitive generators in positive graph cohomology and compatibility with brackets and source grading. Primitive degree-zero injections alone do not pay this map. Primary definitions and general motivic bridges unread.

352007.title: Saturation conjecture for the convex geometric hypergraph $M_1^{(r)}$
352007.literal:
Let $r\ge 3$ and let $H_n^{(r)}$ be the convex geometric hypergraph defined in the source. Write $\operatorname{sat}_\circlearrowright(n,M_1^{(r)})$ for the minimum number of edges in an $M_1^{(r)}$-saturated convex geometric hypergraph on $n$ vertices. **Saturation conjecture for $M_1^{(r)}$.** For all $r\ge 3$ and $n$ sufficiently large in terms of $r$, 

$$
\operatorname{sat}_\circlearrowright(n,M_1^{(r)})=|H_n^{(r)}|.
$$

Moreover, $H_n^{(r)}$ is the unique $M_1^{(r)}$-saturated convex geometric hypergraph achieving this bound provided $n$ is sufficiently large in terms of $r$. The paper proves the corresponding asymptotic lower bound for all $r$ and uniqueness when $r=3$, while the stated exact formula and uniqueness for general $r$ remain open.
352007.derivation_and_gap: Three sustained routes in SUSTAINED-ROUTES.md. Precise gap: uniform exact objective and uniqueness comparison for all r-valid short tuples 1<=l<=r-2; unconstrained semi-valid descent need not preserve r-validity.

356270.title: Generalized connectivity conjecture for matroids with circuits and cocircuits of different cardinalities
356270.literal:
Let $s,t$ be positive integers and let $M$ be a matroid. A matroid is **$(2\min\{s,t\}-1)$-connected** in the usual matroid-connectivity sense; $M\backslash X$ and $M/X$ denote deletion and contraction of a set $X$, respectively. An $(s,t)$-spike is a matroid of the corresponding generalized spike type.

**Generalized connectivity conjecture.** There exists a function $f: \mathbb{N}^2 \rightarrow \mathbb{N}$ such that if $M$ has no circuits of size at most $2s-1$, no cocircuits of size at most $2t-1$, is $(2\min\{s,t\}-1)$-connected, and

$$
|E(M)| \ge f(s,t),
$$

then at least one of the following holds: there exists an $s$-element set $X \subseteq E(M)$ such that $M/X$ is $(s+1)$-connected; there exists a $t$-element set $X \subseteq E(M)$ such that $M\backslash X$ is $(t+1)$-connected; or $M$ is an $(s,t)$-spike.

This is proposed as a generalization of the earlier conjecture, whose symmetric case has circuits and cocircuits of the same forbidden size. The source notes that sufficiently large $(s,t)$-spikes provide the obstruction, but does not report a proof or disproof of the generalized claim.
356270.derivation_and_gap: All s,t matroid minors need a connectivity-preserving s-contraction or t-deletion theorem outside generalized spikes. Circuit/cocircuit size bounds alone do not control separations after several contractions. No structural splitter lemma or infinite obstruction family was obtained.

361013.title: The asymptotic $k/2$ conjecture for directed cycle packing and covering
361013.literal:
Let $k\ge 3$ be fixed. For a directed graph $D$, let $\nu_k(D)$ be the maximum number of pairwise arc-disjoint directed $k$-cycles, and let $\tau_k(D)$ be the minimum number of arcs whose removal makes $D$ free of directed $k$-cycles.

**Asymptotic directed-cycle packing and covering conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex directed graph $D$ satisfies

$$
\tau_k(D)\le (k/2)\nu_k(D).
$$

The conjecture proposes improving the paper's dense-case bound with constant $2k/3$ (and $25/8$ for $k=5$) to $k/2$. It is stated only asymptotically in the number of vertices.
361013.derivation_and_gap: The literal all-large-order bound is unchanged by adding isolated vertices, so a finite violating digraph would amplify; none was constructed. Directed k-cycle hypergraph cover-versus-packing arguments give only factor k automatically. Need k/2 for all fixed k, including directed triangle analogue, not only dense additive-error bounds.

365999.title: Asymptotic equivalence of the edge functions for uniform systems
365999.literal:
Let $r$ and $t$ be integers with $r\geq 3$ and $t\geq r$. For an $(r,t)$-system $(H,\mathcal{F})$, let $e_{r,t}(s)$ be the minimum of $e(H)$ over systems with $|\mathcal{F}|=s$, and let $e_{r,t}'(s)$ be the corresponding minimum over maximal systems. The notation $f(s)\asymp g(s)$ means that the two functions have the same order of magnitude. **Asymptotic edge-function conjecture.** For all integers $r\geq 3$ and $t\geq r$, 
$$
e_{r,t}(s)\asymp e_{r,t}'(s).
$$
 This compares arbitrary and maximal $(r,t)$-systems and predicts that imposing maximality does not change the asymptotic edge requirement.
365999.derivation_and_gap: Three sustained routes in SUSTAINED-ROUTES.md. Same-vertex maximal completion preserves exactly s sets but costs only provably quadratic in e; need a linear-cost replacement for all fixed r,t. Source pays only special cases, no recount.

368090.title: Asymptotic optimizer sequence for the lower bound in $g(n,k,\ell)$
368090.literal:
For each triple $(n,k,\ell)$, let the right-hand side of be the lower-bound expression from Theorem, optimized over the parameter $j$. **Asymptotic optimizer conjecture.** For every $\ell \geq 2$, there is a sequence

$$
0 = \alpha_0(\ell) < \alpha_1(\ell) < \alpha_2(\ell) < \dots < \frac{1}{3}
$$

of real numbers such that, if $n,k$ tend to infinity with $\frac{k}{n} \rightarrow \gamma$ and $\alpha_{i-1}(\ell) < \gamma < \alpha_i(\ell)$, then the right-hand side of attains its maximum at $j=i$.

This predicts a phase diagram for the asymptotically optimal choice of $j$ in the lower-bound construction. The source gives no resolution or supporting result for this assertion.
368090.derivation_and_gap: Three sustained routes in SUSTAINED-ROUTES.md: finite-product binomial-tail limit, adjacent-tail identity, large-index control. Missing globally ordered crossings/no skipped optimizer/uniform growing-j bound and initial-index binding. Wording-only ell>=4 defect earns zero.

375642.title: Asymptotic sharpness of the layered lower bound for Boolean-lattice chain covers
375642.literal:
Let $B_n$ be the Boolean lattice of subsets of an $n$-element set, and let $N(n,r)$ denote the minimum number of maximal chains needed to cover all strict $r$-term chains in $B_n$. For an admissible gap vector $(a_0,dots,a_r)$, meaning $a_0,a_r
e 0$ or $a_0,a_r\ge 0$ and $a_i\ge 1$ for $1\le i\le r-1$, with $a_0+\cdots+a_r=n$, define

$$
M(n,r):=\max_{\mathbf a}\binom{n}{a_0,a_1,\dots,a_r}.
$$

**Asymptotic sharpness conjecture.** For every fixed $r\ge 1$,

$$
N(n,r)=(1+o(1))M(n,r).
$$

The quantity $M(n,r)$ is a layered lower bound obtained by fixing the gap vector of the covered chains. The conjecture is disproved: the exact equality version is false in general, as shown by the paper's discussion of small values.
375642.derivation_and_gap: Exact-equality failure at small n in the literal does not refute asymptotic equality for fixed r. Fractional chain covers have layered lower bound but rounding without multiplicative loss remains unpaid. Primary is unread and no open-status clearance inferred.

380945.title: Andrews–Gordon $q$-series conjecture
380945.literal:
Let $k\geq1$, $1\leq\ell\leq k$, $1\leq i\leq k+1$, $1\leq i'\leq\ell+1$, and $|q|<1$. Let $C_k$ be the Cartan matrix of type $A_k$, let $B_{\ell-1}$ be the inverse Cartan matrix of type $A_{\ell-1}$, and let $\vec{e}_j$ be the standard basis vectors, with $\vec{e}_j=\vec{0}$ for $j\geq k+1$. Define

$$
\vec{Q}_{i,i',\ell}=\vec{e}_i+\vec{e}_{i+2}+\cdots+\vec{e}_{i'}+\vec{e}_{i'+2}+\cdots+\vec{e}_{\ell+1}+\vec{e}_{\ell+3}+\cdots.
$$

Let $r$ and $s$ have the meanings used in the source. **Andrews–Gordon $q$-series conjecture.** The parity-restricted $q$-series on the left-hand side of the statement is equal to the first displayed expression on the right when $r\equiv k\pmod2$, and to the second displayed expression when $r\not\equiv k\pmod2$. These expressions involve sums over $n$, $\vec{\mu}$, and congruence-restricted integers $j$, with the exponents and congruence conditions exactly as displayed in the source. The identities would produce new $q$-series results after replacing $q$ by $1/q$ and taking $L\to\infty$; the source gives no proof or resolution beyond presenting them as conjectures.
380945.derivation_and_gap: Literal omits the two main series and parameters r,s, so exact source recovery essential. No parity-preserving coefficient bijection or finite q-identity supplied. Formalization of a nearby classical Andrews-Gordon theorem would not be the literal target.
